input.summary: Meridian's 241-system estate is operationally critical but analytically fragmented, blocking all five priority use cases.
covers: Tableau, Power BI, SAS analytics estates
Claims administration and pharmacy claims platforms
CRM, contact center, and telephony platform
AWS analytics foundation and Databricks on AWS (target-state direction)

story.meaning: Meridian operates a deeply integrated but analytically siloed application estate — Epic is clinical-of-record, yet claims, pharmacy, finance, and contact center data remain ungoverned and unlinked.
story.observed: Thirteen current-core systems are evidenced across clinical, claims, finance, and member service domains. AWS and Databricks are target-state direction only — no certified medallion architecture, no identity spine, and no governed semantic layer exist in production.
story.matters: Every priority use case — lakehouse, AI/LLM automation, call center optimization, cost transparency, payment integrity — requires cross-system data harmonization that the current estate cannot deliver without foundational governance investment.
story.supports: Closing five evidence gates (medallion architecture, identity spine, semantic layer, transcript governance, contract digitization) is the prerequisite before any use case can advance from planning to decision grade.

findings: Epic Clarity and Caboodle are current-core clinical reporting assets, but no certified medallion architecture connects them to claims or pharmacy — the lakehouse use case cannot advance without this evidence gate closed.

Four parallel BI tools (Tableau, Power BI, SAS, SQL Server marts) produce duplicated, ungoverned metric definitions; this fragmentation directly blocks the governed semantic layer required for AI/LLM automation and cost transparency.

AWS and Databricks are aspirational target-state direction — no production analytics workloads, no Unity Catalog, no Delta integration are evidenced; treating them as current capability is a planning risk.

Contact center and CRM are current-core operationally but lack transcript governance, intent taxonomy certification, and member identity linkage — three of four call center optimization evidence gates remain open.

breakdown.title: Application Estate: Lifecycle Status vs. Use-Case Readiness

rows.label: Current-Core (evidenced, production)
rows.note: Epic suite, claims, pharmacy, CRM, contact center, GL, contracts

rows.label: Fragmented Reporting (ungoverned)
rows.note: Tableau, Power BI, SAS, SQL Server marts — duplicated rules, no semantic layer

rows.label: Target-State Direction (aspirational)
rows.note: AWS analytics foundation and Databricks on AWS — not production-ready

rows.label: Active systems (planning-grade)
rows.note: 224 candidate rows pending classification and evidence closure

rows.label: Evidence gates open across top-5 use cases
rows.note: Medallion, identity spine, semantic layer, transcript governance, contract digitization, and more

chain: Epic Clarity / Caboodle → SQL Server marts → Tableau / Power BI / SAS (fragmented extract chains, duplicated business rules)
Claims administration + Pharmacy claims → SQL Server marts → SAS payment integrity models (ungoverned lineage)
Contact center transcripts + CRM cases → member identity linkage (unproven) → call center optimization use case
Provider contract repository (manual) → GL close reporting → cost transparency use case (blocked by contract digitization gap)
AWS foundation + Databricks → planned medallion lakehouse → all five priority use cases (aspirational, not evidenced)
relationships.note: The SQL Server reporting mart layer is the single most consequential dependency: it sits between every source system and every BI/analytics consumer, yet carries duplicated rules and no certified governance — making it both the current integration hub and the primary blocker for all use-case advancement.

gaps.missing: No certified medallion architecture on AWS/Databricks
gaps.blocks: Unified clinical + claims lakehouse; all downstream AI/LLM use cases
gaps.needed: Bronze/silver/gold layer design, Unity Catalog configuration, and Delta integration evidence
gaps.handoff: Technology Platform and Data Platform owners; evidence gate: MER-V3-EVID-0053, -0054

gaps.blocks: Lakehouse, call center optimization, cost transparency — any cross-domain member-level analytics
gaps.needed: Identity resolution design, MDM or probabilistic matching evidence, and load certification
gaps.handoff: Data Platform and Epic Analytics owners; prerequisite to all five top use cases

gaps.missing: No certified semantic layer or formal data governance operating model
gaps.blocks: AI/LLM automation, cost transparency, payment integrity — any governed metric production
gaps.needed: Semantic ownership assignments, data quality rules, and governance RACI evidenced
gaps.handoff: Enterprise Data Warehouse and Analytics owners; blocks seven use cases per CEO/CFO priority

gaps.missing: Transcript governance and intent taxonomy not certified for contact center
gaps.blocks: Call center optimization — agent assist, next-best-action, AHT/FCR baselining
gaps.needed: Transcript retention policy, QA-label schema, intent taxonomy sign-off, and CRM real-time integration proof
gaps.handoff: Member Services and Member Experience owners; four of four evidence gates open

gaps.missing: Provider contract terms not in governed digital form
gaps.blocks: End-to-end cost transparency and provider quality use cases
gaps.needed: Contract digitization, capitation and VBC term extraction, and attribution ownership certification
gaps.handoff: Network Contracting owner; single largest blocker for cost transparency per CEO/CFO

evidence.name: Epic Suite (Hyperspace, Clarity, Caboodle)
evidence.type: System inventory — clinical EHR and reporting
evidence.facts: All three Epic components are current-core, high-criticality, and evidenced. Clarity and Caboodle feed SQL Server extract chains and Tableau/BI tools. No certified medallion connection to claims or pharmacy is evidenced.
evidence.fields: capability, owner, criticality, lifecycle_status, integrations, data_dependencies
evidence.supports: Lakehouse foundation use case — evidence gate: Epic Clarity medallion architecture must close before use case advances
evidence.missing: Certified medallion architecture; patient/member identity spine; claims and pharmacy harmonization proof

evidence.name: On-prem SQL Server reporting marts
evidence.facts: Classified critical-lifecycle fragmented_reporting_estate. Feeds Tableau, Power BI, and SAS via SSIS/SQL Agent. Carries duplicated business rules across departmental marts. Medium confidence — full scope not yet certified.
evidence.fields: capability, owner, criticality, lifecycle_status, integrations, data_dependencies
evidence.supports: Identifies the primary integration bottleneck blocking semantic layer certification and all governed analytics use cases
evidence.missing: Full mart inventory; business rule deduplication scope; migration sequencing to target-state platform

evidence.name: Claims administration and pharmacy claims platforms
evidence.facts: Claims platform is critical-core (medium confidence); pharmacy platform is high-criticality (high confidence). Both feed SQL Server marts via EDI and NCPDP extracts. Claims/pharmacy harmonization is not proven.
evidence.fields: capability, owner, criticality, lifecycle_status, integrations, data_dependencies
evidence.supports: Payment integrity, cost transparency, and lakehouse use cases — harmonization evidence gate must close
evidence.missing: Claims/pharmacy harmonization proof; vendor identity for claims platform; adjudication rule lineage

evidence.name: AWS analytics foundation and Databricks on AWS
evidence.facts: Both classified aspirational_not_ready. AWS foundation is planned network/security/IAM only. Databricks integration is planned S3/Unity Catalog/Delta — no certified medallion, no production analytics workloads evidenced.
evidence.fields: capability, owner, criticality, lifecycle_status, integrations, data_dependencies
evidence.supports: Confirms target-state direction is not yet a planning-grade foundation; all five use cases cannot rely on this platform without evidence closure
evidence.missing: Medallion architecture certification; Unity Catalog configuration; network/security/IAM foundation completion; production workload evidence

evidence.name: CEO / CFO / CIO stakeholder intent — top use cases
evidence.type: Stakeholder interview evidence — executive priority alignment
evidence.facts: CEO, CFO, and CIO all cite lakehouse, AI/LLM governance, call center optimization, cost transparency, and payment integrity as top priorities. All five are flagged as promising but not decision-grade pending evidence closure.
evidence.supports: Confirms executive alignment on use-case priorities and validates that evidence gate closure — not strategy — is the binding constraint
evidence.missing: Approved business cases; baseline metrics; PHI controls; HITL and audit logging evidence; benefits ledger ties

evidence.name: Contact center, CRM, and provider contract systems
evidence.type: System inventory — member service and network operations
evidence.facts: CRM and contact center are current-core but ungoverned for analytics. Provider contract repository is current-manual — terms not in governed digital form. Transcript governance, intent taxonomy, and member identity linkage are all unproven.
evidence.fields: capability, owner, criticality, lifecycle_status, integrations, data_dependencies
evidence.supports: Call center optimization and cost transparency use cases — four of four evidence gates open for contact center; contract digitization is the single largest cost transparency blocker
evidence.missing: Transcript retention policy; QA-label schema; intent taxonomy certification; contract digitization scope and timeline

visual_blocks.title: Application Readiness vs. Use-Case Advancement
visual_blocks.subtitle: Each cell shows whether the system is ready (✓), aspirational (⚠), or a confirmed blocker (✗) for the top-5 use cases. Evidence gates must close before any ✗ or ⚠ cell can advance.
